profile.reading: OptimumHQ, marketed as OptimumAI, is a software company that builds AI-powered ERP, CRM, and business-automation tools for small and midsize businesses. The company's own website lists its office at 70 South Val Vista Drive in Gilbert, Arizona, while the address on file for this listing is 1955 South Val Vista Drive in neighboring Mesa. Val Vista Drive runs through both cities, so the discrepancy may reflect a past office location, a mapping error, or a different suite in a shared complex. Either way, OptimumHQ is a software business rather than a data center or colocation operator, and nothing publicly available indicates server or data center infrastructure at either address.
profile.research_note: Confirmed via optimumhq.com that OptimumHQ (OptimumAI) is an AI-powered ERP/CRM/business-automation software company, not a data center. Its own site lists 70 South Val Vista Drive, Gilbert AZ as its address, differing from the OSM-tagged 1955 South Val Vista Drive, Mesa AZ (stored coordinates 33.3804149, -111.7526684); Val Vista Drive runs through both cities. Reverse geocode of the stored coordinates returns only the bare Mesa address with no business name, and the same address separately appears associated with another unrelated registry row, consistent with a shared multi-tenant building rather than a dedicated data center. This address is several miles from the other 8 rows in this batch, so no single shared building connects all 9. Treated as a mistagged OSM telecom=data_center point.

reading.body:
This record cannot be read as a data center campus. The OpenStreetMap entry tagged as OptimumHQ at 1955 South Val Vista Drive, Mesa, refers to OptimumAI, a software company that builds enterprise resource planning and customer relationship management tools. The operator's own published address is 70 South Val Vista Drive, Suite A3-120, in neighboring Gilbert, Arizona, not Mesa. No data center specifications, power capacity, or colocation services are published for this location.

The registry maps 56 facilities across Arizona, of which only four have published power capacity. This entry cannot be ranked or compared to the state's published capacity of 512 megawatts, as no power figure exists for it.

This site does not assert operator, capacity, or colocation status for this entry. The OpenStreetMap record appears to be a miscategorization of a software vendor's office address rather than a genuine data center facility.
